_readme: feekah source list. 'topic' must match a topic id in the app: family, health, nature, science, kindness, culture, humor. 'tier' decides how hard an item has to work to get in — see _howItWorks. Run 'node validate-feeds.mjs' to check everything, '--write' to save status back here.

_howItWorks.tier1: Pre-filtered sources. Someone else already decided this outlet publishes constructive news. An item is included unless the blocklist catches it. This is a light safety net, not the main filter.
_howItWorks.tier2: General news wires. No editorial filter upstream, so the logic is inverted: an item must EARN inclusion, either by carrying a category in 'categoryAllow' or by matching a word in 'require'. Anything that clears neither bar is dropped. Order of evidence, strongest first: sectionBlock (the URL's own section) → categoryBlock (the publisher's own tag) → block (title keywords) → categoryAllow or require. Publisher metadata beats keyword guessing every time and should always be preferred where a feed provides it. Far fewer items survive, and the failure mode becomes 'boring' rather than 'a conviction for abusing a child' — which is the trade you want for a calm morning read.
_howItWorks.block: Matched against the TITLE ONLY, using the language's matchMode. Matching against the summary too was dropping good stories: 'Taking the stairs could protect your heart' died because its summary mentioned a heart attack. Keep this list about crime, death and disaster — not about topics.
_howItWorks.allow: Rescue phrases. If the title contains an allow phrase, any block word that sits inside that phrase is forgiven. This is what lets 'heart attack' through while 'terror attack' still dies.
_howItWorks.require: Tier 2 only. Positive signal, matched against the title. KEEP TOPIC NOUNS OUT OF THIS LIST. The first live run proved the rule: every leak came from a topic noun and none from an action word. 'skog' admitted a house fire ('Villa i skogen brann') and a forest-fire story ('skogsbränder'); 'festival' admitted a piece about teenage drinking; 'lösning' admitted one about drug scenes; 'musikk' admitted a funding withdrawal. A topic noun says what a story is ABOUT, which is exactly the thing that carries no sentiment — 'skog' appears in both a woodland-restoration story and a wildfire. Only verbs and outcomes belong here: räddar, hjälper, firar, oppdaget, breakthrough. Honest limitation even then: keyword matching is a blunt instrument for sentiment, and it kills good stories as readily as bad ones. NOTE: an LLM classifier is NOT an option — feekah must stay AI-free at fetch time, consuming no tokens per day. So when tier 2 underperforms, the fix is better publisher metadata (categoryAllow, sectionBlock) or a narrower section feed URL — never a model. On the first run with categories wired in, tier 2 went from 0 usable Norwegian items to 13.
_howItWorks.dedup: The validator drops cross-source duplicates within each edition, by normalised title and by canonical URL. VG and Aftenposten are both Schibsted and genuinely do run the same story.
_howItWorks.matchMode: 'substring' for Norwegian and Swedish, 'word' for English. Norwegian and Swedish compound their nouns, so a blocked stem often sits at the END of a word — 'tarmkreft', 'brannvesen', 'riksdagsval' — and word-boundary matching sails straight past it. English does not compound and needs the boundary, or 'dead' swallows 'deadline'. The cost of substring mode is that short stems collide: bare 'val' in Swedish matches val (whale), valp, valross and kvalitet, so the lists below use 'riksdagsval' and 'valrörelse' instead. Keep NO/SV entries at four characters or more and check them against a compound before adding.

sources.name: forskning.no
sources.note: 168 items. Labrador CMS exposes RSS through a query parameter, not a path — every /rss.xml, /feed and /rss guess 404s or returns HTML, which is why this was written off as dead. Do not 'fix' this URL to something tidier.

sources.name: ung.forskning.no
sources.note: 118 items. forskning.no's science site written for children and young readers — plain language, and squarely aimed at the everyday-family brief.

sources.name: NRK Viten
sources.note: Science section. Reliably calm. Blanks its <description> on most items, so these arrive as title-only cards.

sources.name: NRK Nyttig
sources.note: Home, health, money, training tips. Best single fit for the everyday-family brief.

sources.name: NRK Kultur
sources.note: Tier 2 despite being a culture section: it carries artist obituaries and industry scandals.

sources.name: NRK Vestland
sources.note: Regional feeds carry the local human-interest stories, and also every local fire and drowning. Swap for your own region.

sources.name: NRK Nordland
sources.note: Sent summaries on 1 of 20 items last run. If requireSummary is ever turned on, this source effectively disappears.

sources.name: VG
sources.note: General wire. No category tags worth using (only Sport/Nyheter/Rampelys), but the URL carries the section: 6 of 10 items were vg.no/sport/. Blocking sport and rampelys (celebrity) leaves the nyheter items to the keyword gate.

sources.name: Aftenposten
sources.note: No category tags at all, but the URL carries the section. A sample run was verden(7) sport(5) norge(5) meninger(4) e24(2) oslo(1) karriere(1) — so opinion, business and world news are blocked by section, leaving norge/oslo/karriere for the keyword gate. Much of Aftenposten is subscriber-only and RSS gives no way to detect it (see _paywall); readers will hit walls.

sources.name: Natursidan
sources.note: Swedish nature and wildlife. Almost entirely positive by nature.

sources.name: SVT Nyheter Väst
sources.note: This is the feed that put a child abuse conviction and a fatal boat accident through the old blocklist. Tier 2 exists because of this source.

sources.name: Positive News
sources.note: Constructive journalism, UK. Closest in spirit to feekah.

sources.name: sciencenorway.no
sources.note: 233 items. forskning.no in English — same Labrador CMS, same ?lab_viewport=rss trick. Gives the EN edition a Nordic angle instead of only UK/US sources.

sources.name: Atlas Obscura
sources.note: Curious places, odd history, delightful footnotes. Feeds the humor/oddities chip without being a joke site.

sources.name: Oddity Central
sources.note: Weird-but-true. Tier 1 but watch it: 'oddity' sometimes means grim rather than funny, so the blocklist is doing real work here. Check its samples after each run.

_paywall.note: The paywall filter was REMOVED, and should not be added back in this form. It was heuristic detection of subscriber-only items via title prefixes ('VG+', '+') and category tags ('pluss', 'premium'). Dumping VG's real RSS proved it detects nothing: items carry <vg:waplink>, <vg:img>, <vg:body/> and a <category> that only ever reads 'Nyheter' or 'Sport'. There is no premium marker in the feed at all. The old config reported '0 paywalled (excluded)' out of 10 on VG and 0 out of 25 on Aftenposten while appearing to work — a silent no-op, which is worse than no filter, because it looks like protection. If you want paywall filtering, it has to come from fetching the article URL and checking the page, not from RSS.
_paywall.sportNote: Sport results in a general feed read as neutral or bad news to whoever lost. The tier-2 require lists deliberately exclude 'vinner'/'vant'/'seier' and their Swedish equivalents for this reason. If you keep sport, prefer feature and human-interest sections over results.

_broken.note: Confirmed dead. Probed directly rather than assumed — do not re-add without a URL that actually returns items.
_broken.forskning-no: https://www.forskning.no/rss.xml → 404. Also tried /feed (404), /rss (200 but HTML), and forskning.no without www (404). The /rss page exists and is titled 'RSS', but it runs Labrador CMS and renders its feed list client-side, so the real URLs are not in the HTML. Open https://www.forskning.no/rss in a browser and copy the actual feed links — this is the single highest-value fix for the Norwegian gap.
_broken.sciencenorway: https://www.sciencenorway.no/rss.xml → 404. Also tried /feed and /rss (both 404). Same Labrador CMS as forskning.no; same browser step needed.
_broken.ung-forskning: Suggested as a new Norwegian source (forskning.no's science site for young readers). Tried /rss.xml and /feed — both 404. Needs the same browser discovery.
_broken.janegoodall: https://news.janegoodall.org/feed/ → HTTP 200 but returns HTML, not a feed. Parsed 0 items. Removed.

_removed.vg-godt: Removed as a duplicate. 'https://www.vg.no/rss/feed/?format=rss&categories=godt' returned byte-identical items to the plain VG feed — the categories parameter is ignored, so it was one source counted twice, not a food section.

_wanted.note: Gaps worth filling. The Norwegian gap is the urgent one: after removing dead feeds, NO has exactly two tier-1 sources against five tier-1 sources in English.
no: Local paper for your own kommune

_policy.note: Bounded reading is the product, not a performance tuning knob. feekah's sun arc fills as you scroll and ends at 'that's the good news for today'; an edition of 300 stories turns that ending into a lie and rebuilds the infinite scroll the app exists to avoid. maxPerTopic caps each topic separately rather than the edition overall, so a reader who picks one chip still gets a full read instead of whatever was left after a dominant topic ate the budget.
